successors.name: Wu (state)
successors.text: Xu's heartland, 'conquered by Wu in 512 BC'; King Zhangyu surrendered and 'Hereby, Xu was extinguished'

ledger.x: c. 1042: the Xu of the Huai River valley first appear in the record, in the Rebellion of the Three Guards against the Duke of Zhou. 'Xu's existence is first reliably reported by the Yi Zhou Shu for 1042 BC'; infobox 'Established: Unknown', foundation stories 'remain legendary'. The page says Xu was 'centered in…
512: Wu conquers Xu and the state ends.

wars.name: Zhou subjugation of the Huai valley (Rebellion of the Three Guards)
wars.outcome: Xu 'participated in the Rebellion of the Three Guards against the Duke of Zhou'; Zhou forces subjugated the Huai valley in 1039.

wars.name: Xu-led Huaiyi coalition against Zhou
wars.outcome: 'By 944 BC, Lord Yan of Xu managed to unite thirty-six Dongyi and Huaiyi states'; the Zhou 'could not re-subjugate the Huaiyi' and accepted their independence; the Huaiyi counter-offensive of 850 collapsed; King Xuan's campaign of 822 ended in a minor Zhou…

wars.name: Chu invasion of Xu and Battle of Loulin
wars.outcome: 'Chu retaliated in 645 BC, and launched an invasion of Xu'; Qi's coalition failed to relieve Xu at Loulin, but Xu survived, weakened.

wars.name: Wu conquest of Xu
wars.outcome: Wu under King Helü besieged Xu; King Zhangyu surrendered and Xu was extinguished.

certainty.note: Xu's extent is known from bronzes and a few city names; the Huai valley frontier of 944 is the widest and least certain.
